title: The gatekeeper
blurb: A walled manor with a porter, a steward and a groom. Get inside, by any way at all.
after: Every way in was earning, persuading or daring. The city at the end of the road will ask the same.
refines: Which routes do players find? Do the porter's rule, the steward's grounds and the breach each work end to end?

steps.title: Ashby Manor
cards: …signal. A walled manor. Godwin the porter keeps the gate; Steward Merrick decides who comes in; Ned the groom has the steward's ear.
Everything you've practised counts here: talk, deeds, deals, someone's word, what you make, and what you dare. There's more than one way in.
There's no one right way, and no words to copy. The device helps if you ask (H).

steps.title: Inside
steps.done: Inside. Every way in was a way of earning, persuading, or daring: the same choices the city will ask.
help: Godwin has his own reasons for letting people through. The steward wants a reason and someone's word. Ned has a job going.
Walls have weak places, too. But what you damage, people may see.

playtest.say: Good morning. Is there any work I could do? I'd like to get into the manor.

playtest.do: stitch the snapped cheek strap of the halter back to its buckle with the waxed leather thong

playtest.say: Good day, Steward. Ned will tell you I mended the mare's halter. The house is short of hands for the feast: may I come in and work?

2.do: cut a way through the brambles in the gap of the old wall with the billhook

try_also: sew the broken halter strap back together with the thong
